name: Connie Chan
summary: As SF Supervisor, voted 8-3 for Gaza ceasefire resolution: sustained ceasefire, humanitarian aid, hostage release; condemned Oct. 7 Hamas attack and Netanyahu government's attacks on civilians.
quote: Preston, Ronen and Ahsha Safaí were among the supervisors who spoke in support of the measure and voted for its passage, along with Peskin, Melgar, Connie Chan, Joel Engardio and Shamann Walton.

name: Connie Chan
summary: In Mission Local foreign-policy interview, pledged to co-sponsor Block the Bombs Act, saying Netanyahu government has violated human rights and committed war crimes.
quote: I would co-sponsor the Block the Bombs Act with the understanding that the [Benjamin] Netanyahu government, at this moment, has violated human rights and committed war crimes, and the United States should not be aiding that effort.

name: Connie Chan
summary: On Iron Dome funding, took conditional rather than outright-ban framing: any US defensive-system funding must be packaged with Gaza aid and ceasefire compliance mandates.
quote: If and when the U.S. Congress continues to provide funding for Iron Dome, it has to be part of a package to provide aid for food and medicine for Gaza, and to mandate the Netanyahu government to comply with the ceasefire terms and conditions.

name: Connie Chan
summary: Drop Site reported AIPAC's UDP and DMFI funneled ~$500K to a super PAC network (EDW Action Fund / Pro-Choice Majority Action) that bought ads supporting Chan; her campaign denied receiving any AIPAC money.
quote: Connie has also been clear from day one of this campaign that she would not accept a dime from AIPAC and she has stayed true to this throughout.

name: Connie Chan
summary: J. found AIPAC/DMFI money went to independent PACs, not Chan's campaign; recapped her record: called for end of military aid to Israel, condemned Gaza war as genocide, supported Block the Bombs Act.
quote: She has called for the end of military aid to Israel, condemned Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza as genocide against Palestinians and supported the Block the Bombs Act.

name: Connie Chan
summary: Told The Intercept she will oppose all US aid to Israel and stop its 'genocidal actions'; also opposes US involvement in Israel's invasion of Lebanon and said she'd have voted for the failed House war-powers withdrawal resolution.
quote: In Congress, we will oppose any aid to Israel and do everything in our power to stop their government's genocidal actions against the Palestinian people.

name: Connie Chan
summary: Signed Track AIPAC's candidate questionnaire affirming Israel is committing genocide against Palestinians, backing a total arms embargo on Israel, and requiring AIPAC to register as a foreign agent; accepted its endorsement.
quote: Connie has signed our candidate questionnaire, affirming that Israel is committing genocide against the Palestinian people and that Congress must end U.S. complicity in it and hold those responsible to account.

name: Connie Chan
summary: Campaign website standing pledge (site footer, all pages): will not take money from corporate PACs, AIPAC or its lobbyists and representatives.
quote: Connie Chan for Congress will not take money from corporate PACs, AIPAC or its lobbyists and representatives, the NRA or lobbyists and executives from pharma, PG&E, fossil fuel or tobacco companies.

name: Connie Chan
summary: In televised debate days before ballots mailed, called for full arms embargo on Israel, said she'd vote day one to end 'a genocide in Gaza and an apartheid state,' and would not fund Iron Dome.
quote: Chan said that "on day one in Congress" she would vote to "end a genocide in Gaza and to end an apartheid state."

name: Connie Chan
summary: After opponent Scott Wiener was confronted by pro-Palestine activists at the Trans March, her spokesperson deferred to his experience rather than condemn protesters: solidarity 'against hate whenever someone tells us they are experiencing hate.'
quote: In this moment, what matters is how State Senator Scott Wiener felt and feels about the interactions. We must stand in solidarity against hate whenever someone tells us they are experiencing hate.
